name: Compute Pressure
plain: Reports how stressed the CPU is (nominal, fair, serious, critical).
meaning: Coarse load level; shows if the device is struggling. Can leak what else is running.

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Reports how stressed the CPU is (nominal, fair, serious, critical).

limits.headline: Can see how busy your device's chip is, but not exact numbers
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when a heavy app or call is open, if the site is allowed.
can: Learn if your chip is in one of four states: nominal, fair, serious or critical
Slow a video call or game when the device is hot
Check while the page is open and in front
cannot: See exact usage numbers or temperatures
See what other apps are doing
Work in Firefox, Safari or on iPhone
Keep checking after you close the page
limits.differs: Only desktop Chrome and Edge support it. Firefox, Safari and Android browsers do not.

story.what_it_is: A page can learn how busy your computer's processor is.

marketing.name: Compute Pressure API
marketing.pitch: Chrome's docs describe it as a way to see CPU load in simple levels so apps can adapt.

story.for_you: You never see it. A video call or a game may lower effects when your computer is busy, so it keeps running smoothly.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to adapt: drop video quality, turn off background blur, lower graphics. It also gives them a hint about how powerful and loaded your device is.

use_cases.example: A call app turns off background blur when your processor is overheated.
A browser game lowers its effects when the computer is under heavy load.
A web editor lowers preview quality when you export in the background.
A streaming tool drops resolution before your stream stutters.
A fraud tool reads load changes as another hint that a device is real.
An ad system picks lighter ads on a device that is struggling.

technical_bounds: No Android, no Firefox, no Safari
